Priya: Provide sandbox setup script + minimal benchmark (due 2025-11-13)

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We're joined by Priya our solution engineer and Liam from devad, do I have that right?
[00:08] Tom: Yep Tom here, CTO. Marta's on too.
[00:12] Marta: Hi, sorry a little late at the start.
[00:15] Jordan: No worries. Quick agenda: 1) stack / constraints; 2) we do a live SDK quickstart in both Python and TS; 3) show the Console and Optimize suggestions; 4) next steps and pilot scope. Sound good?
[00:29] Tom: Sounds perfect. We're mainly trying to understand host vs dedicated and costs and how quickly our engineers can get to a reliable integration.
[00:38] Priya: Great. Marta, can you briefly describe Riverbank's current inference flow for summarization?
[00:43] Marta: Sure. We build nightly ETL that extracts large doc sets and run a summarization job — right now it's using a self-hosted smaller model behind k8s, but latency is spiky and cost tuning has been a pain. We also have compliance needs for a subset of data.
[00:57] Priya: Got it. Do you have an SLO for tail latency or token cost?
[01:02] Marta: We want 95th percentile under 600ms for short prompts and cost under $0.0008 per token for production queries if possible.
[01:10] Priya: Okay noted — that helps shape batching/quantization suggestions.
[01:15] Jordan: Quick qualification: timeline and evaluation criteria for the pilot?
[01:20] Tom: 4–6 week pilot, outcome: consistent latency under SLO for typical queries and cost delta vs current infra. Stakeholders include infra, data science, and security.
[01:31] Jordan: Great — we'll scope for that.
[01:33] Priya: Alright, moving to the SDK quickstart. I'll share my screen and walk through a repo we sent. Link in chat: https://redwood.example/sandbox/riverbank-quickstart (note: placeholder).
[01:45] [Screen share noise]
[01:47] Priya: First the Python flow. pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var. In CI we recommend using secrets manager instead of plain envs — we document GitHub Actions and GitLab snippets.
[02:02] Marta: For local dev, do you recommend per-dev API keys or a shared sandbox key?
[02:07] Liam: For sandbox we usually issue a shared ephemeral key per team, but for production use service accounts + RBAC so you can rotate keys without redeploy.
[02:16] Nia: How does the service account auth work with VPC/private deployments? Our infra team wants KMS-backed keys and audit logs.
[02:23] Priya: In Private mode we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and we provide audit logs in the control plane; we also support SAML SSO and SCIM for admin provisioning. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:33] Jordan: Note: we'll include the SOC2 + ISO docs and private deployment checklist.
[02:37] [02:38] Priya: Back to code — quick snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate("Summarize the following ..."); prints(resp.text) — typical flow.
[02:52] Eli: Is the SDK synchronous only? We have streaming consumers for long-form generation.
[02:57] Priya: There's streaming support in both py and ts SDKs; streaming uses chunked responses and you can hook into partial tokens to update UI. We'll paste examples.
[03:07] [03:10] Priya: Now TypeScript quickstart: npm i @redwood/sdk; set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const res = await client.generate({ prompt: '...' });
[03:20] Marta: Any gotchas around CORS or browser keys?
[03:24] Liam: For browser apps we advise using a short-lived token minted by a backend service; don't embed long-lived keys in client-side bundles. There's an example exchange flow in the docs.
[03:34] Tom: Ok — for pilot we plan to run both a batch ETL and a low-latency API route. How do you handle routing?
[03:42] Priya: Routing is policy-driven — you can prefer hosted for dev and dedicated for production, or route based on latency/cost region. We also support fallbacks: if a GPU pool is busy, requests can fall back to a compatible quantized variant.
[03:56] Marta: Is quantization transparent or do we need to change prompts?
[03:59] Priya: It's transparent to the API — but there can be small quality tradeoffs, which is why we include model recommendation profiles and evals tied to your prompt set.
[04:10] [04:12] Jordan: Quick Console tour: I'll push control to Priya to show the per-route dashboards — latency percentiles, token cost breakdown, and token-level cost heatmaps.
[04:20] Priya: Here you can see a per-route cost tab, route configs (batch sizes, concurrency), and Optimize suggestions which will recommend batch size and when to enable KV caching for prefix-heavy workloads.
[04:33] Nia: Does the Optimize feature run offline simulations or live traffic analysis?
[04:38] Priya: Both. It uses historical traces to simulate cost/latency and then recommends safe defaults; you can also run a real-time experiment to validate.
[04:46] Eli: Any built-in tests for quality regressions when swapping quantized models?
[04:50] Priya: Yes—we tie eval suites to prompt sets and raise alerts if quality drops exceed thresholds. You can run these in CI so every deployment triggers a regression check.
[04:59] [05:02] Tom: About compliance — what logs do we get for Private? We need tenant-level audit and exportable logs for our auditors.
[05:09] Priya: Private provides customer-managed control plane with exportable audit logs, KMS integration, and optional on-prem bundles. For Hosted we provide access logs and redacted payloads depending on plan. We'll attach the exact log schemas.
[05:23] Tom: Great. On pricing, we expect a line item for reserved capacity if we want dedicated pools.
[05:29] Jordan: Yes — hosted is usage-based, dedicated is reserved monthly commit with optional burst; I'll include both cost scenarios in the SOW.
[05:37] Marta: For the pilot, we want to run a 2‑week benchmark first with the provided script. It should test latency distribution for our typical prompt mix and a throughput run for nightly jobs.
[05:49] Priya: We'll provide a minimal benchmark script and a sandbox with sample data. The script will produce p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-inference numbers.
[05:58] [06:01] Jordan: Quick note: we should map success metrics: p95 < 600ms, cost < $0.0008/token for typical queries, and regression delta < 1% on quality score. Marta, agree?
[06:12] Marta: Yes that's what we'll sign off on.
[06:15] Nia: Network questions — if we go Private inside our VPC, do you require open egress? We have strict egress policies.
[06:22] Priya: For on-prem we can run the inference plane inside your network; for Private cloud we need control-plane connectivity optionally over a narrow management endpoint. We can support air-gapped with the on-prem artifact.
[06:33] Tom: Any trial credits or sandbox GPU time?
[06:36] Jordan: We'll allocate sandbox credits; Priya will provision a small dedicated GPU for benchmark runs.
[06:40] [06:41] Priya: One more thing: CI secrets — we recommend using ephemeral service account tokens and rotating them; example GitHub action is in the repo.
[06:50] Marta: For the SDK, how do we instrument cost per route? We want token-level chargebacks for teams.
[06:56] Priya: The Console exposes token counts per API key and per-route; Combine that with tagging and you'll get chargeback reports. You can also export to your billing system via CSV or webhook.
[07:08] Eli: Does Redwood support embedding generation and similarity search? We ultimately want that too for retrieval-augmented workflows.
[07:13] Liam: Yes — we support text embeddings, vector store integrations, and reranking endpoints. We'll share integration examples for Pinecone/FAISS.
[07:22] [07:25] Jordan: Ok let's recap and confirm next steps.
[07:28] Tom: Quick clarifying Q — in the TS SDK will types be stable across minor versions? We care about lockstep type safety.
[07:36] Liam: We publish semver and changelogs; for major infra changes we tag migration notes. In pilot we'll recommend pinning minor versions in package.json.
[07:45] Marta: One more — can we get a small sample of the audit log schema? Our compliance engineer needs to review.
[07:51] Jordan: We'll attach the schema in the follow-up.
[07:54] [08:00] Priya: I'll summarize the repo steps in a checklist in the follow-up: 1) clone repo, 2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY, 3) run quickstart script, 4) run benchmark with your prompt set.
[08:12] Nia: Can you also include the network diagram for Private deploy?
[08:16] Priya: Yes.
[08:18] Jordan: Any more questions?
[08:20] Marta: Not from me, thanks that was really practical.
[08:23] Tom: Thanks, good session.
[08:25] Jordan: Great — we'll send SOW and security pack. Proposed pilot kickoff next Monday 2025-11-17. Thanks everyone.
[08:33] [call ends]
